security_spec.violation_condition: In XiangShan RTL, the PMP CSR write logic in the mseccfg CSR module does not enforce the sticky-bit behavior of mseccfg.MMWP and mseccfg.MML. Specifically, after either bit transitions from 0→1, a subsequent CSR write (CSRRW/CSRRS/CSRRC) targeting mseccfg that attempts to clear these bits succeeds—the hardware writes the new value without blocking the 1→0 transition. The PMP reset signal (which should be the only mechanism to clear these bits) is not gating the write-enable of these sticky fields. This violates the spec requirement that MMWP and MML 'cannot be unset until a PMP reset.'
security_spec.summary: mseccfg.MMWP and mseccfg.MML are sticky bits that must remain set once written to 1, only clearable by PMP reset; hardware that allows software CSR writes to clear these bits after they are set enables M-mode to silently escape Smepmp lockdown, reverting to permissive M-mode memory access

findings.finding: MML (bit 0), MMWP (bit 1), and RLB (bit 2) are declared as RO(0) — the ROType class uses wfn=wNoEffect, meaning every CSR write to these bits is silently discarded. Software can NEVER set MML=1 or MMWP=1. The spec (machine.adoc §norm:mseccfg_mml_sticky, §norm:mseccfg_mmwp_op_warl) requires these to be WARL sticky bits: writes of 1 must take effect, writes of 0 must be ignored (blocking the 1→0 transition) until a PMP reset. The hardware is not just lacking sticky semantics — it refuses ALL writes, making Smepmp entirely non-functional.
findings.snippet:
val RLB   = RO( 2).withDescription("Rule-locking bypass control from the Smepmp extension.")
val MMWP  = RO( 1).withDescription("Machine-mode whitelist policy control from the Smepmp extension.")
val MML   = RO( 0).withDescription("Machine-mode lock-down control from the Smepmp extension.")

spec_citations.excerpt: The mseccfg.MMWP is a WARL field. This is a sticky bit, meaning that once set it cannot be unset until a PMP reset. ... The mseccfg.MML is a WARL field. This is a sticky bit, meaning that once set it cannot be unset until a PMP reset.

findings.finding: ROType.wfn is hardcoded to wNoEffect (line 46) and CSRModule line 38-39 does case ROType(_) => (empty — no update logic), meaning any CSR write is silently discarded with zero side effects. There is no 'sticky WARL' field type in the codebase — one whose write function checks the current register value and blocks 1→0 transitions unless a PMP reset signal is asserted. Without such a type, the spec's required sticky-bit behavior for MML and MMWP cannot be implemented.

findings.finding: `val passThrough = if (pmpEntries.isEmpty) true.B else (mode > 1.U)` — M-mode (mode=3.U) unconditionally gets passThrough=true, granting full r/w/x to every non-locked PMP region. Per Smepmp spec §3.2, when mseccfg.MML=1, M-mode must be checked identically to S/U mode — no passThrough, no ignore. This passThrough computation has zero dependency on MML state.

When mseccfg.MML is set ... M-mode-only rule is enforced on Machine mode and denied in Supervisor or User mode.

findings.finding: The default PMP entry (fallback when no rule matches) assigns r=w=x=passThrough. For M-mode this yields allow-all (r=w=x=1). Per Smepmp §norm:mseccfg_mmwp_op_warl, when MMWP=1 with MML=1, the default policy for unenumerated regions must be deny-all. This unconditional allow-all default is a privilege-escape vector.
findings.snippet:
val pmpDefault = WireInit(0.U.asTypeOf(new PMPEntry()))
pmpDefault.cfg.r := passThrough
pmpDefault.cfg.w := passThrough
pmpDefault.cfg.x := passThrough

spec_citations.excerpt: The mseccfg.MMWP ... changes the default PMP policy for Machine mode when accessing memory regions that don't have a matching PMP rule. When set it changes the default PMP policy for M-mode ... to denied instead of ignored.

findings.finding: PMPCheckerEnv carries keyIDen, cmode, mode, pmp, pma — but no MML, MMWP, or RLB fields. The PMP checker hardware has zero visibility into Smepmp configuration. This is architecturally impossible to fix with CSR changes alone — the PMP check data-path itself needs a widening to carry Smepmp state from CSR→TLB→PMP checker.
findings.snippet:
class PMPCheckerEnv(implicit p: Parameters) extends PMPBundle {
  val keyIDen = Bool()
  val cmode = Bool()
  val mode = UInt(2.W)
  val pmp = Vec(NumPMPReal, new PMPEntry())
  val pma = Vec(NumPMAReal, new PMPEntry())

spec_citations.excerpt: This extension introduces the RLB, MMWP, and MML fields in the mseccfg CSR and their associated rules.

findings.finding: Only PMM (bits 33:32) is wired to the TLB: `io.tlb.pmm.mseccfg := RegNext(mseccfg.regOut.PMM.asUInt)`. The symbols mseccfg.regOut.MML, .MMWP, .RLB are never referenced — nor could they be, since the TlbCsrIO.pmm.mseccfg port is only `UInt(2.W)` (line 217). Smepmp configuration bits have no hardware path to the PMP checker.

findings.finding: The PMPChecker composes pmp_match_res + pma_match_res + keyid_check + pmp_check. None have Smepmp awareness: (a) no MML-gated passThrough/ignore/default control, (b) no Smepmp Table 3 RWX encoding re-interpretation in pmp_check, (c) no MMWP-driven default-deny whitelist, (d) no RLB bypass control for locked entries. The entire PMP enforcement path is Smepmp-unaware.
findings.snippet:
val res_pmp = pmp_match_res(...)(check_addr, req.size, io.check_env.pmp, io.check_env.mode, lgMaxSize)
val resp_pmp = pmp_check(cmd, res_pmp.cfg)
val resp = if (pmpUsed) (resp_pmp | resp_pma | resp_keyid) else (resp_pma | resp_keyid)

findings.finding: `val ignore = passThrough && !pmp.cfg.l` — for M-mode (passThrough=true), every non-locked PMP entry grants full r/w/x. In Smepmp with MML=1, non-locked (S/U-mode-only) PMP rules must deny M-mode access, not grant it. The ignore signal lacks any MML-gating.
findings.snippet:
val ignore = passThrough && !pmp.cfg.l
val cur = WireInit(pmp)
cur.cfg.r := aligned && (pmp.cfg.r || ignore)
cur.cfg.w := aligned && (pmp.cfg.w || ignore)
cur.cfg.x := aligned && (pmp.cfg.x || ignore)

spec_citations.excerpt: An S/U-mode-only rule is enforced on Supervisor and User modes and denied on Machine mode.
